text:
jen: Quick intake — customer (FinX) asked for per-tenant SLOs for response quality + retention guarantees. Trying to capture problem, goals, non-goals, and clear acceptance criteria so eng/product can prioritize.

jen: Problem statement: FinX needs predictable behavior when they route high-volume traffic to Dedicated. Today they see intermittent quality regressions after model rollouts and spikes in cost due to repeated tokenization across many short chats. They asked for: per-tenant min-quality SLOs, retention window guarantees, and automatic fallback when quality drops.

maria: thx jen. can you share the exact customer SLO targets they mentioned?

jen: they asked for >= 95% pass rate on their in-house eval set (per-hour rolling) and 7-day retention of embeddings for recall features. also want failover to a cheaper model if quality < 92% for 10m.

akshay: sketching tradeoffs: per-tenant SLOs mean extra instrumentation + storage for per-tenant evals and retention. fallback policies are doable but we need clear acceptance criteria to avoid flip-flop.

tim: agree — also need to decide cost budget. If we keep 7-day retention in-memory for fast recall it increases RAM/GPU cache size. Is FinX willing to pay for Reserved capacity bump?

jen: FinX said they're open to a billing uplift as long as we can show 20–30% improvement in tail latency and no more than 5% incremental cost on avg.

nina: non-goals request: this intake should NOT include building a tenant-specific model. Also not solving long-term model drift detection across global tenants — that's separate.

akshay: suggested approach: 1) instrument per-tenant evals feeding from FinX's eval set (hosted on their S3). 2) implement a quality monitor and a canary + fallback policy (roll to fallback after 10m sustained failure). 3) retention configurable per-tenant with default 7 days, option to pay for longer.

maria: can we call out edge cases? e.g., noisy eval labels, low-volume tenants where stats are unstable, and cross-tenant caching leading to leakage concerns.

akshay: good call. propose minimum volume threshold (>= 100 eval queries per hour) to apply SLO; below that we use asymptotic smoothing and surface warnings instead of automatic rollback. Also ensure tenant isolation for cached embeddings (namespace keys).

jen: writing acceptance criteria draft — please react and edit inline: 

```
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Per-tenant quality SLOs: system computes pass_rate on FinX eval set hourly. For tenants with >=100 eval queries/hour, pass_rate >= 95% for a rolling 1h window.
- Automatic fallback: if pass_rate < 92% for 10 consecutive minutes, route new requests to configured fallback model within 30s; record rollback events to console and customer dashboard.
- Retention: default embeddings retention = 7 days; configurable per tenant. API accepts `retention_days` when creating tenant config.
- Cost guardrails: system emits estimated monthly cost delta for changes; default policy requires FinX opt-in for >10% cost increase.
- Privacy/isolation: cached embeddings and KV namespaces are tenant-scoped; no cross-tenant cache hits.
- Telemetry: dashboard shows pass_rate, recent rollbacks, retention usage, and cost estimates; alerts to FinX and Redwood SRE on sustained failures (>30m).
```

jen: pls thumbs up if this matches product intent, or suggest changes. :eyes:

maria: :thumbsup: one note — fallback apply latency target 30s seems tight if model spin-up needed. maybe 2min default with fast-path if warmed pools available.

akshay: +1 to 2min default. we can expose `fallback_grace_period` param and try to pre-warm when rollout detects failures.

tim: add acceptance test: simulate model degradation and validate fallback triggers and no more than N% user-facing error increase. we should add `error_rate < 1%` as regression guard.

nina: edge-case: what if FinX disables fallback (opt-out) but still expects alerts? need explicit per-tenant toggle.

jen: noted. final asks before I convert to PRD/RFC? priorities: 1) confirm acceptance criteria text, 2) agree on default fallback timeout (2min), 3) confirm billing uplift gating (>10% opt-in).

maria: I can draft the metrics dashboard mock and eval ingestion flow. akshay — can you estimate engineering lead time (rough)?

akshay: rough estimate: 6w for monitoring + fallback plumbing (small team), +2w for retention config + 2w for dashboard. assume parallel work -> ~8–10w end-to-end with QA and rollout.

jen: perfect. i'll update the PRD with these ACs and schedule a 30m sync with FinX. thanks all.
